Possible ways: Guinness World Record at Nashik Kumbh 2027Research

Research and possible ways only. Nothing here is final or approved.

Scope, record ideas, process, cost and timeline for a KDM phone-charging record at the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh.

Key findings (research, not final)

We found no existing Guinness record for charging phones at an event, so there is room for KDM. Guinness does not publish its full database, so this is not 100% confirmed until we apply.

A record counted across the whole mela (many points over many days) would not pass Guinness rules as written. The attempt must be one measurable number at one location in a fixed time.

One possible fit for the Kumbh: one solar + battery KDM station that charges the most phones in 24 hours. It needs little space, pulls no extra crowd, and solves two real problems: dead phones and power cuts.

If KDM goes ahead, an early start (Oct to Nov 2026) with the Guinness Consultancy team helps, because approvals and Guinness rules take months.

1. Has anyone done this before?

What we checked What we found
Phone charging at an event No Guinness record found in our search. Guinness does not publish its full database, so this is not confirmed until we apply.
Phone records by brands Yes, but about phones themselves, not charging. Example: HONOR's record for the most phones dropped at the same time (2025).
Guinness records at Maha Kumbh 2025 Yes, set by the Mela Authority: largest river clean-up, most volunteers in a cleanliness drive, handprint paintings, and a synchronised sweeping drive with about 15,000 workers.

2. What Guinness accepts

Guinness only accepts a record title that is all of the following:

  • Measurable: counted or measured, never opinion (no "best" or "biggest initiative").

  • Breakable: someone else can try to beat it later.

  • Standardisable: the same rules apply to anyone who attempts it.

  • Verifiable: proven with video, witnesses, logs and documents.

  • Single variable: only one thing is measured, such as most, largest or fastest.

  • World-beating: it beats an existing record, or meets a tough minimum that Guinness sets for a new title.

Records involving harm, risk or discrimination are rejected. Being first to suggest an idea does not guarantee approval.

What this means for us: adding up 1,080 points over 45 days across the whole mela is risky, because it is many places over a long time. One station, one day, one number is much stronger.

3. Possible scope at the Kumbh

Conditions we set: the record must happen inside the Kumbh, need little space (no big ground), be about charging, and solve a real pilgrim problem. These titles are our suggestions, not confirmed Guinness titles. Guinness will set the final rules and the minimum number.

Possible titles at a glance

Possible title How it would work Fit for Kumbh
Most mobile phones charged at one time, one location One large KDM hub, with a single count of phones charging at the same moment Good, but a big hub pulls a crowd to one spot, so permission is harder
Most mobile phones charged at one venue (station) in 24 hours One hub on an Amrit Snan day, with QR or token logging of every phone Strong fit. Uses the existing flow of pilgrims (see Idea 1)
Largest mobile phone charging station Counted by the number of working charging ports in one structure Good. Can be compact if ports are stacked
Largest solar-powered phone charging station Same as above, but powered by solar, fits the Green Kumbh theme Good. Also solves power cuts
Most mobile phones charged by a solar-powered station in 24 hours Solar + battery station, every phone logged over 24 hours Strong combined option (see Idea 3)
Largest vehicle-mounted mobile charging station Most charging ports on one vehicle Good. Needs no ground at all (see Idea 2)

All titles above are our suggestions, not confirmed Guinness titles. Guinness sets the final rules and minimum numbers.

Idea 1: Most phones charged at one station in 24 hours

Point Detail
Title idea Most mobile phones charged at a single charging station in 24 hours
Problem solved No pilgrim stays with a dead phone at the busiest point on an Amrit Snan day.
Space One KDM kiosk or tent.
Crowd No extra crowd. Pilgrims already passing by charge their phones, so police permission is easiest.
Proof QR or token entry for every phone, CCTV, independent witnesses.
Watch out Guinness will define what "charged" means (for example minimum minutes or battery %). The system would need to be built to that rule.

Idea 2: Mobile charging van

Point Detail
Title idea Largest vehicle-mounted mobile charging station (most charging ports on one vehicle)
Problem solved Charging moves to where the crowd is: holding areas, parking, and the tight lanes of Trimbakeshwar.
Space One vehicle. No ground needed.
Bonus Keeps working for the whole mela after the record, and acts as a moving brand hoarding.
Proof Count of ports, all shown working at the same time.

Idea 3: Off-grid solar + battery station

Point Detail
Title idea Most mobile phones charged by a solar-powered station in 24 hours
Problem solved Power cuts in the monsoon. In July 2026 the Godavari crossed the danger mark and power poles fell. This station runs without the grid.
Space One kiosk.
Bonus Fits the Green Kumbh theme, which makes it easier to pitch to NTKMA.
Watch out Less sun in the monsoon, so the battery bank must be large. Engineering must be tested first.

One possible combination (not final)

Possible main attempt: combine Ideas 1 and 3. One solar + battery KDM station that charges the most phones in 24 hours. It covers the charging problem, the power-cut problem and the green angle in one attempt, with a small footprint and no crowd pull.

If Guinness rejects the solar title, plain Idea 1 could be the fallback.

Idea 2 (charging van) could be a separate, smaller attempt that can be done in one day.

Other options we considered

Option Why it is a backup option
Largest human image of a charger or the Bharat Ka Charger logo Very visual, but needs a large ground and draws a crowd. Better outside the mela, for example at a Nashik college ground.
Largest mosaic made of chargers or cables Strong product visual, but does not solve a pilgrim problem.
Largest functional charger, or longest working charging cable Fun for reels, but weak on problem-solving.
Most chargers or phones collected for recycling in one week Fits the plastic-free, clean Kumbh plan and has a CSR angle. Good second record.
Partner on NTKMA's own record attempts At Prayagraj the Mela Authority set records itself. KDM could join as sponsor or tech partner at lower cost.
India Book or Asia Book of Records Cheaper and easier, but much less prestige than Guinness. Backup only.

4. Process and cost

Route Details
Business route (KDM's route) Guinness sends companies to its paid Consultancy service. It includes a fast-tracked application and an official Adjudicator who verifies the attempt on the day and can hand over the certificate on the spot. Price is not public; a quote has to be requested from Guinness.
Standard route Free. A new title proposal has a $5 processing fee. Up to 12 weeks to assess the application, then up to 12 weeks to review evidence. No adjudicator.
Priority upgrade New title: $1,000 (£650). Existing title: $800 (£500). Processed in 5 working days. Not refunded if rejected.
Logo use Using the Guinness logo in ads needs a separate licence fee.
Volume Guinness receives over 50,000 applications a year, so waiting times can grow.

Possible steps

  1. Contact Guinness Consultancy (account manager) and share the record ideas.

  2. Guinness reviews the title. If accepted, it sends official guidelines and the minimum number to beat.

  3. Get permission from NTKMA and the police for the attempt site and date.

  4. Build the station and the counting system to Guinness rules. Do a test run.

  5. Book the adjudicator, run the attempt, and collect all evidence.

  6. Adjudicator confirms the result on the day; certificate handed over.

5. Possible timeline (working back from 2 August 2027)

When What to do
Oct to Nov 2026 (now) Contact Guinness Consultancy. Choose the final title. Ask NTKMA for permission for the attempt.
Dec 2026 to Jan 2027 Submit the application. Receive the official rules and minimum number.
Feb to Apr 2027 Design the station, build the counting system, line up independent witnesses.
May to Jun 2027 Test run at a smaller event.
Jul 2027 Book the adjudicator. Set up the station before the mela peak.
Attempt day 31 Aug 2027 (2nd Amrit Snan), with 11 Sep 2027 as backup. 2 Aug is risky as the first big test day.

6. Risks

Risk How to handle it
Permission NTKMA and police may block anything that draws a crowd on a peak day. Choose an attempt that uses the existing flow of pilgrims, and get written permission first.
Rejection by Guinness The title may not be accepted. Keep a backup title ready (plain Idea 1, or the van).
Monsoon Rain and power cuts on the day. Use battery and solar backup and a second attempt date.
Competition Pepsi (Sting) also offered charging at Prayagraj and could try a similar record. Moving early matters.
Cost Consultancy fee is unknown until Guinness quotes. Get the quote before committing.

7. Possible next steps

  • Founders choose the main idea and the backup.

  • Send an enquiry to the Guinness Consultancy team and request a quote.

  • Add the record attempt to KDM's CSR proposal to NTKMA.

  • Engineering team checks how many phones one solar + battery station can charge in 24 hours.

Possible ways: live phone counting (KDM Smart Socket)Research

Research and possible ways only. Nothing here is final or approved.

How every KDM charging box at Nashik Kumbh 2027 can count each phone it charges, automatically, with the real KDM charger in front of the pilgrim.

Key findings (research, not final)

Yes, it is possible. Each KDM box (5 to 6 single-port chargers) gets a metered socket behind every charger and one small controller inside the box. The KDM charger stays fully visible and unchanged.

One limit: power alone cannot always tell “phone full” from “phone removed”. The fix is to count a phone only when the socket data and a QR token scan agree, with CCTV as a third check.

Built for many small boxes: every box counts on its own and stores data offline, so adding more boxes only adds more points, not more complexity.

Possible timeline: lab test now, pilot with 5 boxes in Dec 2026 to Jan 2027, live by 15 July 2027, Guinness attempt on 31 August 2027.

1. Is it possible? Yes, with one fix

A metered socket measures the mains power each charger draws. A charger with no phone draws very little; a charger with a phone draws several watts. That jump is easy to detect, so each charging session can be counted automatically.

The limit: when a phone reaches 100% or is unplugged, power falls in both cases. Counted on power alone, a full phone that tops up again could be counted twice.

The fix: three layers that check each other.

Layer What it proves Role in the count
Metered socket (automatic) Real charging happened: start, duration, energy (Wh) Proves each session was real charging
QR token (attendant app) One phone handed in and handed back, linked to a socket Sets session start and end; one token = one count
CCTV (one per cluster of boxes) Visual record of handovers Spot checks and Guinness evidence

A phone counts only when a token session and a matching power session agree. Guinness must still confirm this evidence format is acceptable (section 10).

2. System overview

Each box counts its own phones and sends the data over 4G; the cloud adds up all boxes and feeds four screens.

Figure 1. Data flow from the KDM charger to the dashboards

The QR token app and CCTV sit outside the box, so the box itself stays small. If the network fails, the box keeps counting and sends everything later.

3. The KDM charging box

One possible design keeps the current small box with 5 to 6 plug points and adds counting parts inside it. Part names are common examples; the engineering team or vendor picks the final parts.

Part Per box What it does Notes
KDM single-port charger 5 to 6 Charges one phone; fully visible and branded One charger = one phone = one socket
Metered socket 5 to 6 Measures each charger's mains power about once a second Pilot: off-the-shelf smart plugs with energy metering. Scale: one 6-socket board with a metering chip per socket (BL0942 or HLW8012 class)
Box controller 1 Reads all sockets, detects sessions, stores logs ESP32-class chip with SD card and battery-backed clock
4G module 1 Sends data to the cloud Small LTE module with a data SIM; stores and resends if the network is jammed
Small battery backup 1 Keeps the controller and counting alive in power cuts Sized for the controller; chargers can stay on grid
Safety parts 1 set Protects pilgrims and staff 30 mA RCCB, MCB, earthing, IP54 or better enclosure
QR labels 5 to 6 One label per socket: box ID + socket number Printed, weatherproof

Why single-port chargers matter: the socket sees one charger's total power, so one active charger always means one phone.

Power per box: at about 20 W per charger, 6 chargers draw about 120 W plus a few watts for the controller. Check against the real KDM charger rating.

Safety: the metering chips sit at mains voltage, so the board must be fully enclosed. Pilot units should use BIS-certified off-the-shelf parts where possible.

Connecting many boxes: two options

Option How it works Good for Watch out
A. 4G in every box (suggested) Each box has its own 4G module and SIM Boxes spread across parking, ghats, stations; each box works alone One SIM per box; data cost grows with box count
B. Zone hub Boxes in a cluster send over short-range radio (Wi-Fi or LoRa) to one hub with 4G Many boxes close together, such as a holding area Hub is a single point of failure; more setup

Option A looks simpler for a pilot. Option B may suit places where 10 or more boxes stand together.

4. Scaling up: more boxes, more phones

Small boxes make it easy to add points. The table shows what different box counts could mean, using Prayagraj 2025 usage as the guide.

KDM boxes Charging points (6 per box) Phones per day, rough
150 900 about 37,000
300 1,800 about 74,000
500 3,000 about 1.2 lakh

How this is estimated (our calculation, not confirmed): KDM reports over 20 lakh phones in 45 days through 1,080 charging points at Prayagraj. That is about 41 phones per point per day on average. Nashik crowds, box locations and peak days will change this. The pilot will give the real number.

What scaling needs besides boxes:

  • Attendants: one attendant per 2 to 3 boxes for token scans and phone safety; more on Amrit Snan days.

  • CCTV: one camera per cluster of boxes, not one per box.

  • Spares: about 10% spare boxes, chargers and controllers at each zone for quick swaps.

  • Placement: holding areas, outer parking, railway waiting halls and medical points (see the Kumbh research page).

5. Counting logic

The box controller turns power readings into charging sessions, then matches each to a QR token. Thresholds below are starting values to tune in the pilot and align with Guinness rules.

How a power session is detected

  1. Read each socket's power every second.

  2. Start: power stays above the start threshold (for example 1.5 W) for 10 seconds. An idle charger usually draws far less; confirm on real KDM chargers.

  3. During: add up energy (Wh) and time.

  4. End: power stays below the end threshold (for example 0.8 W) for 60 seconds.

  5. Merge: a new start on the same socket within a few minutes, with the same token, is the same phone topping up, not a new phone.

When a phone is counted

  • A QR token was scanned in and out for that socket.

  • At least one power session falls inside that token window.

  • The session meets the minimum rule (for example at least 10 minutes or a minimum Wh). Guinness defines what "charged" means; the system takes it as a setting.

Edge cases

Situation What the socket sees How it is handled
Phone reaches 100% and stays plugged in Power falls to a trickle, may rise again Merged into one session while the token is unchanged
Phone removed early Power falls to idle Counted only if the minimum rule is met
Power bank or other device Power draw like a phone Attendant check at handover + CCTV; unusual patterns flagged
Faulty charger No power or constant draw Socket marked faulty on the dashboard; charger swapped
Power cut Readings stop Controller battery keeps logs safe; session closed and flagged
Token not scanned Power session with no token Not counted; listed for supervisor review
Network down Nothing reaches the cloud Box keeps counting and storing; uploads later

6. QR token and CCTV

Token flow at each box

  1. Each socket has a QR label (box ID + socket number).

  2. Pilgrim hands over the phone. Attendant gives a numbered token card and scans the token and the socket label in the app.

  3. Phone is plugged into the KDM charger on that socket.

  4. On return, the attendant scans the token again; the session closes and the phone goes back.

  5. The token also stops phones going to the wrong person.

Attendant app requirements

  • Works offline and syncs later.

  • Scans in under 2 seconds, with large buttons for busy hours.

  • Collects no personal data: no name, no phone number. This keeps it simple under India's DPDP Act 2023.

  • Optional later: a WhatsApp "phone ready" alert, which would need the pilgrim's number and consent.

CCTV

  • One camera per cluster of boxes, covering the handover points.

  • Recording kept locally and copied to the cloud daily.

  • Used for spot checks against token logs and as Guinness evidence on the attempt day.

7. Software

Part What it does Example tools
Box firmware Reads sockets, detects sessions, stores logs, uploads when online ESP32 firmware, logs on SD card
Messaging Sends box data to the cloud and resends anything missed MQTT over TLS (encrypted), store-and-forward
Cloud data store Holds every reading, session and token from all boxes Managed MQTT broker + Postgres or time-series database
Operations dashboard Live map of boxes, sockets in use, faults, counts per box and hour Grafana or a simple web app
Public counter One big live number for LED screens and social media Simple web page
NTKMA view Read-only box map and load for the mela command centre Same dashboard, limited access
Evidence pack Every counted phone with time, socket, energy and token CSV export + daily hashes

Tamper-evident logs: each box writes an append-only log. Each day's log gets a cryptographic hash (a digital fingerprint), sent to the cloud and shared with the auditor the same day. If anyone edits a record later, the hash no longer matches.

Time: every box keeps time with a battery-backed clock and syncs when online. Each record carries box time and upload time.

How live: with the network up, data reaches the dashboard in about 1 to 2 minutes. During network jams it arrives late but complete.

8. Possible build path

One possible path: prove the counting with off-the-shelf parts in a 5-box pilot, then build the 6-socket board, and go live by 15 July 2027.

Figure 2. Five phases and two gates to go-live

Gate 1: sensor and token counts must agree in the pilot before building at scale. Gate 2: Guinness confirms the evidence format before rollout. If the custom board is not ready by May 2027, roll out the off-the-shelf sockets proven in the pilot.

9. Rough cost per box (to verify)

A pilot box with off-the-shelf parts costs roughly ₹15,000 to ₹48,000, excluding chargers. These are approximate market ranges from general knowledge, not vendor quotes; get at least two quotes before budgeting.

Item (per 6-socket box) Qty Rough range (₹)
Metered smart sockets, off-the-shelf 6 6,000 to 15,000
Box controller (ESP32-class board, SD card, clock) 1 1,000 to 9,000
4G module or small router 1 2,000 to 8,000
Small battery backup 1 3,000 to 8,000
Enclosure, RCCB, MCB, wiring, earthing 1 set 3,000 to 8,000
Total per box about 15,000 to 48,000

Not included: KDM chargers, mobile data (about ₹300 to ₹600 per SIM per month), CCTV per cluster, cloud hosting, software development and testing, attendants.

At scale: a custom 6-socket board should cost less per box than six off-the-shelf plugs, but needs design, testing and certification time. Ask a vendor to quote both.

10. Risks and open questions

The biggest risk is whether Guinness accepts this evidence format, so ask them first.

Risk Impact Mitigation
Guinness does not accept sensor data Count may not qualify Ask in the first call; token log + CCTV as main proof, sensor data as backup
Charger idle power close to trickle False starts or ends Lab-test real KDM chargers; tune thresholds
Many boxes to maintain Faults go unnoticed Dashboard flags faulty sockets; spares at every zone
Network jams at peak Dashboard lags Offline storage + resend; count complete even if late
Monsoon water and heat Short circuits, failures IP54+ boxes, raised stands, RCCB, spare units
Attendants skip scans when busy Real phones not counted Simple app, training, extra staff on Amrit Snan days
Electrical approval delays Boxes not allowed to run Apply early through NTKMA and MSEDCL with the safety plan

Questions for Guinness

☐ What counts as one "charged" phone: minimum time, battery %, or energy?

☐ Is a QR token log + metered power data + CCTV accepted as evidence?

☐ How many independent witnesses are needed, and who can be one?

☐ Can the attempt run across many boxes and locations in 24 hours?

Questions for KDM engineering or vendors

☐ Idle and charging power of the chosen KDM single-port charger.

☐ Can the in-house team build the 6-socket board, or should a vendor?

☐ Which metered plugs are BIS-certified for a public pilot?
